routes.name: Visa-Free Stay
routes.summary: Citizens of countries on the Decision on Visas list can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Treaties can change this for some countries. Report your stay within 48 hours if you plan more than 3 days and are not in paid accommodation or with a host.

other: Country list is in the Decision on Visas. The exact list was not read.

sources.label: Service for Foreigners' Affairs: types of residence

routes.name: Temporary Residence Permit
routes.summary: Issued for up to one year, on grounds like marriage, family reunification, education, work, being a company founder, humanitarian reasons, or owning real estate. First application is usually filed at a BiH embassy or consulate.

other: Inside BiH you can only apply first if you entered on a long-term D visa or are from a visa-free country.
Overstaying can mean a 300 to 1,500 KM fine, deportation and a 1 to 5 year entry ban.

routes.name: Employment Under a Work Permit
routes.summary: Your employer gets a work permit from the Employment Agency first. Then you apply for temporary residence. You can't work until residence is granted, and only in the job on the permit.

sources.label: Service for Foreigners' Affairs: types of residence

stay.note: Permit validity plus 30 days, but not more than one year.

routes.name: Residence for Marriage or Family Reunification
routes.summary: Temporary residence for spouses or partners of BiH citizens and for family reunification.

other: Specific conditions and durations not read.

routes.name: Temporary Residence for Education
routes.summary: Temporary residence for students. Only half the time on a study permit counts toward permanent residence.

routes.name: Permanent Residence
routes.summary: Needs 5 years of continuous temporary residence. Absences up to 10 months total, or one up to 6 months, still count. You need income, housing, health insurance, a clean record and basic knowledge of an official language.

eligibility.language: One of the official languages and scripts (exempt: children, over 60 not working, or those schooled in an official language)
other: Adequate accommodation and health insurance in BiH.
Criminal record certificates from home country and BiH.
